summary: Iteration 7 backend+frontend verification. Backend pytest: 86/86 passed (74 regression + 12 new: 9 admin-edit-user, 3 form-email-link). UI E2E: admin can create user, edit non-admin (name+email), duplicate-email correctly rejected (400 toast + row unchanged), admin's eu-role select is disabled when editing an admin user. Forms: creating a form with recipient email succeeds and toast reads 'Form saved — email not sent (email not configured)'; form appears in list with copy-link. Patient auto-fill behaviour verified in code (onPatientSelect sets recipient_email from patient.email).
ui_flows_verified: Admin login -> Team -> Add User (uf-name/email/password/role -> save-user-btn) creates new user in list.
Admin -> edit-user-<id> opens modal with eu-name/eu-email/eu-role/eu-password. Editing name+email persists to list (list reflects new email + name).
Duplicate email save (target=doctor@vpp.com) returns 400 (browser console shows 400) and row keeps prior email — no overwrite.
Editing admin@vpp.com row: eu-role select is disabled (verified via el.disabled === true).

Forms -> New Form (add-form-btn) shows new ff-recipient field with hint 'If provided, the patient is emailed the secure form link.' Filling ff-recipient + title and submitting produces toast 'Form saved — email not sent (email not configured)' and the form appears in the list. Form save NEVER fails when email unconfigured.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now 858 lines — still growing. Split into routers strongly recommended before next feature iteration.

PUT /api/users/{uid}: admin can promote another user's role to 'admin' (only blocks demoting existing admins). This is likely intentional but worth confirming with product — you may want to restrict creation/promotion of new admins.
send_email() logs no error on SMTP failure other than returning False. Consider logging the exception at WARN so ops can distinguish 'not configured' from 'send failed'.

recipient_email is validated with EmailStr but link_base is a raw str — a malformed link_base like 'javascript:' would still be embedded in the email body. Since caller is server-side and value comes from window.location.origin, low risk, but consider URL-validating link_base.
Form email body is plain-text only; no HTML/i18n. Acceptable for MVP.
Frontend Forms.js emailNotSent/emailSent toasts depend on client-side flag from response — good. Consider also surfacing d.recipient_email in the row so staff can see who was contacted.
